target_customer: Robotics builders: household robotics, humanoid, robot arm and quadruped teams, plus defense customers, who want US-made electronics and actuators
problem: Robot teams must buy parts overseas and build the rest in house just to get something moving. HLabs sells a plug and play set of US-made robotic primitives to speed early development.
business_model: Hardware product sales (preorders of boards, motors and actuators) plus bespoke design work for larger production robots
product_category: Robotics components: compute boards, wireless modules, motor controllers, motors and actuators

founders.name: Paul Hetherington
previous_startups: Mystic (YC W21), CEO for six years, outcome not found in sources opened
founders.background_notes: Second time YC founder per the YC page. Education not stated on the YC page.

competitors.name: Unitree
competitors.what: Chinese maker of low cost robot actuators, quadrupeds and humanoids, the benchmark for component price
competitors.traction_then: Joint actuators averaging about 300 dollars each per one analysis

competitors.name: Westmag
competitors.what: US startup making electric motors and actuators, though a article says most of its parts are made in China

technical_complexity.rationale: Motor controllers, boards and actuators are standard but need tight tolerances and quality control; a March 2026 feature noted that manufacturing at scale needs capital. A one person team was building them in house.

defensibility.rationale: Components are copyable by well funded rivals and Chinese suppliers are far cheaper; SemiAnalysis estimated a US built arm costs about 2.2 times more. A US-made angle could help if policy restricts imports.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found in sources. The FCC banned imports of new foreign humanoid and quadruped models in July 2026, which supports demand for domestic parts.

market_need_then: US robot teams depend on China for parts. Policy moved against Chinese robot imports in 2026 and distributors such as RoboStore pivoted to US production, indicating demand for domestic supply. HLabs customer traction is not independently verified.

branding.domain_note: Uses hlaboratories.com rather than hlabs.com; no purchase history found

identity.voice_and_tone: Site title says Make More Robots; plain and direct

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand or community found. Many unrelated companies share the name H Labs.

outcome_analysis: HLabs is an active W26 company with a solo second time YC founder selling US-made robot electronics and actuators. It rides a 2026 policy shift away from Chinese robot imports, but scale, cost against Chinese suppliers and capital are open risks. No outcome events were found.
notes: Funding unverified: Standout and Nordic9 list a 500K seed from Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund (Preqin says an undisclosed seed in 2025-11); no primary source, so not recorded as a round. YC page confirms Founded 2025, team size 1. Outcome search found no layoffs, acquisition or shutdown. Competitor source dates are from 2026 coverage near the batch.
